extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents, associate agents, and registered foreign practitioners dealing with the Canadian Patent Office
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing who may represent applicants and patentees before the Canadian Patent Office, how appointments and revocations of patent agents and associate agents are made, default/common representative rules, and which persons may perform specific actions in prosecution, fee payment, transfers, and related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application formatting and part presentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of the application must be presented in a way that allows the Patent Office to easily process, scan and read the parts of the application; sections 47 to 52 of the Patent Rules set requirements relating to page margins, line numbering, line spacing, font size, page numbering and identification of trademarks; each part of the application must begin on a new page and other requirements relating to drawings and formulas must be met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts are non-compliant the Office may identify a defect in an Office letter or an examiner’s report. See chapter 2.02.02 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent agent licence requirement to represent before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agents are individuals who hold a patent agent licence or a patent agent in training licence issued by the College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents; this licence allows patent agents to represent applicants, patentees and other clients before the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office recommends that all persons submitting a patent application consult a licensed patent agent for advice, regardless of whether the Patent Rules require them to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patent Agents and College oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register of Patent Agents is managed by the College of Patent Agents and Trademark Agents; requirements to obtain and maintain a patent agent licence are set by the College and the College may suspend, revoke or accept surrender of licences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Patent Office relies on the College to supply updated information about new entries and status changes, and revocation/suspension by the College results in revocation of appointments before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to update agent contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent agents must immediately notify the Patent Office of their new address if they move or change firms; changes to preferred method of correspondence for any particular patent application or patent must also be communicated to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not rely on the College to obtain agents’ contact information, so failure to update may cause Office errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status and limitations of registered foreign practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered foreign practitioners are persons recognized as patent agents under the laws of a country other than Canada and have limited ability to act under Canada’s Patent Rules; they are not considered 'patent agents' for the purpose of the Patent Rules or this Manual and cannot be appointed in respect of an application, patent or other business before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To act on behalf of an applicant or patentee, a registered foreign practitioner must (1) be explicitly allowed to take the requested action under the Patent Rules, (2) be given authorization by the applicant/patentee as specified in the Rules, and (3) be listed on the College’s list of registered foreign practitioners. See chapters 5.05 and 5.07 for specific actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and role of a common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: The common representative is a joint applicant or joint patentee entitled to act on behalf of the other joint applicants/patentees in some actions before the Office, particularly the appointment of patent agents; where there are joint applicants/patentees, one will be the common representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint applicants/patentees may collectively appoint one person as common representative; otherwise one will be deemed appointed by default in accordance with the Patent Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of common representative at filing or PCT national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-PCT applications the common representative may be appointed in the petition included in the application on the filing date; for PCT national phase applications the common representative may be appointed in the request for national phase entry or in a notice submitted to the Commissioner at national phase entry date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appointments do not require a signature (paragraph 26(3)(b) and (c) of the Patent Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of common representative by notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A common representative may be appointed at any time during the life of an application or patent by a notice to the Commissioner signed by each of the other joint applicants or joint patentees (paragraph 26(3)(a) of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any previous appointment is revoked by the appointment of a new common representative (subsection 26(12)). The Office recommends appointing the common representative in the petition or request for national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative default appointment rules (applications and PCT/divisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no common representative is appointed, one joint applicant/patentee will be deemed appointed by default according to ordered rules: for non-PCT applications the first person named in the petition, or first named in another single document, or if none then alphabetically first; PCT and divisional have corresponding rules (paragraphs 26(4) and subsection 26(5) etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception rules apply where corrections to naming of applicants or decisions under section 31 of the Patent Act change identities; flow charts in the Manual illustrate these rules and how corrections/decisions affect defaults (subsection 26(6)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Common representative by default once patent granted
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who was the common representative immediately before the patent was granted will remain the common representative once the patent is granted unless the joint patentees make a new appointment under paragraph 26(3)(a) of the Patent Rules (subsection 26(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same applies for reissued patents (subsection 26(8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of transfers on appointment of common representative
rubrics_metrics.description: When a transfer of rights to an application or patent is recorded under section 49 of the Patent Act, the appointment of common representative is affected if full rights of the common representative are transferred; if full rights are transferred to one transferee that person is deemed appointed as common representative; if transferred to multiple transferees, the transferee whose name appears first in the request is deemed appointed (subsection 26(11)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rights of a single applicant/patentee are transferred and after transfer there are multiple applicants/patentees there must be a common representative; rules describe who is deemed appointed in those cases (subsections 26(9) and related). Flow charts illustrate determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appoint a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Any applicant, patentee or third party may appoint one patent agent, or all of the patent agents at a given firm to represent them in their business before the Patent Office (subsection 27(1) of the Patent Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of third party activities include filing a protest or requesting re-examination. Appointment of 'patent agent' may refer to one agent or all of the agents at a firm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to appoint a patent agent (when mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant must appoint a patent agent to represent them if they are not the inventor; if there are multiple applicants and not all of them are inventors they must appoint a patent agent; an appointment is required when a transfer of rights under section 49 has been recorded by the Commissioner (subsection 27(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner’s notice to require appointment of patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner will send a notice requiring that a patent agent be appointed within three months if one is required and none is appointed (subsection 31(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are joint applicants the notice will be sent to the common representative. Failure to appoint within the prescribed time will result in deemed abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for appointment of patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent agent may be appointed at filing or national phase entry or by notice at any time; any appointment is effective on the date received by the Patent Office and must include the patent agent’s name and postal address. If all agents at a firm are appointed, the firm name and postal address suffice (section 29).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all agents at a firm are being appointed it is not necessary to list individual agents; an indication of intent to appoint the firm or all agents is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of patent agent in petition or PCT national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-PCT applications appointment may be made in the petition if included on the filing date; for PCT national phase applications appointment may be made in a notice submitted on or before national phase entry; for divisional applications in the petition on presentation date (paragraphs 27(3)(b),(c),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appointments do not require the signature of the single applicant or the common representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of patent agent by notice — signature and authorization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent agent may be appointed at any time by a notice to the Commissioner. For applicants/patentees the notice must be signed by the applicant/patentee or by a registered foreign practitioner authorized to do so; if signed by a registered foreign practitioner, a document authorizing them must accompany the notice (paragraph 27(3)(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of joint applicants/patentees the notice must be signed by the common representative or an authorized registered foreign practitioner, with authorization documentation. A person appointing a patent agent for other business may sign themselves or authorize a registered foreign practitioner (subsection 27(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent of the patent agent to appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent agent must consent to their appointment; if the appointment document is submitted by the agent, consent is implied; if submitted by someone other than the agent, the appointment is not effective until evidence of the agent’s consent is received (subsection 27(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter from the agent stating agreement (which may be generic and require no signature) or an electronic communication constitutes evidence of consent. If all agents at a firm are appointed, the letter may be written by any of the agents at the firm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default appointment of patent agent continuing for resulting patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment of a patent agent to represent applicants is deemed to also have been made for the resulting patent unless the appointment states otherwise (subsection 27(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid Office errors in tracking appointments limited to the application phase, the Office encourages submission of instructions when the appointment should cease/revoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default appointment of patent agent on transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent agent appointed to represent the applicant or patentee is deemed to have been appointed to represent a transferee when a transfer of an application or patent is recorded by the Commissioner under section 49 unless the request to record the transfer states otherwise (section 30).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of appointment of patent agent — requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of a patent agent may be revoked by notice submitted to the Commissioner; for applicants/patentees the notice must be signed by the agent (any agent if the appointment pertains to all agents at a firm), or the applicant/patentee, or by a registered foreign practitioner authorized to revoke with an accompanying authorization document (subsection 27(7)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For joint applicants/joint patentees the notice must be signed by the common representative or authorized registered foreign practitioner with authorization documentation. A person revoking for other business may sign themselves or authorize a registered foreign practitioner (subsection 27(8)). An appointment is automatically revoked if the agent’s licence is suspended, revoked or surrendered by the College; if all agents at a firm have licences suspended, revoked or surrendered, appointment of all agents is automatically revoked (subsections 27(7) and (8)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed appointments and revocations for members of firms (appointed patent agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all agents at a firm are appointed, then: an agent who becomes a member after the initial appointment is deemed appointed as of the day they become a member; a firm member who later becomes a patent agent is deemed appointed as of the day they become a patent agent; if an agent ceases to be a member their appointment is deemed revoked as of that day; if an agent’s licence is suspended/revoked/surrendered their appointment is deemed revoked as of that day (section 28.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appointment of other agents at the firm remains intact unless all agents' licences are suspended/revoked/surrendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate patent agent — definition and appointment power
rubrics_metrics.description: An associate patent agent is an agent appointed by the appointed patent agent; a patent agent may appoint one associate or all of the patent agents at the same firm to act as associate patent agents in respect of an application, patent or other business (subsection 28(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appointment of an associate agent can be made by the individual appointed patent agent or, where all agents at a firm are appointed, by any one of those agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment content and timing for associate patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: An associate patent agent may be appointed at the time of filing/national phase entry or by notice at any time; any appointment is effective on the date received by the Patent Office and must include the associate agent’s name and address; if appointing all agents at a firm the firm name/address suffices (section 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of associate patent agent in petition or PCT national phase entry
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-PCT applications appointment of an associate may be in the petition if included on filing date and submitted by a patent agent; for PCT national applications appointment may be in a notice submitted by a patent agent on or before national phase entry; for divisionals in the petition on presentation date if submitted by a patent agent (paragraphs 28(3)(b),(c),(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent being appointed as associate may submit the documents themselves; these appointments do not require a signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of associate patent agent by notice — signature rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An associate patent agent may be appointed by a notice to the Commissioner signed by the appointed patent agent; if all agents at a firm are appointed as patent agent any of the agents at that firm may sign the notice appointing the associate (subsection 28(3)(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Default appointment of associate patent agent for resulting patents
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment of an associate patent agent by the appointed patent agent is deemed to have been made for the resulting patent unless the appointment states otherwise (subsection 28(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office encourages agents to submit instructions when they wish the appointment to cease/revoked to avoid tracking errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of appointment of associate patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of an associate patent agent may be revoked by notice to the Commissioner signed by the appointed patent agent or the associate agent; if all agents at a firm are appointed any of those agents may sign the revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment of associate agent is automatically revoked when appointment of the patent agent is revoked. An associate agent’s appointment is automatically revoked if their licence is suspended/revoked/surrendered; similarly for all agents at a firm if all licences suspended/revoked/surrendered (subsections 28(5) and (5.1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed appointments and revocations for members of firms (associate patent agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all agents at a firm are appointed as associate agent: an agent who becomes a member after initial appointment is deemed appointed as of that day; a member who later becomes a patent agent is deemed appointed as of that day; if an agent ceases membership their appointment is deemed revoked; if an agent’s licence is suspended/revoked/surrendered their appointment is deemed revoked (section 28.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appointment of other agents at the firm remains intact unless all agents' licences are suspended/revoked/surrendered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Succession of patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent agent withdraws from practice another patent agent may establish themselves as the successor under section 32; the successor is deemed appointed as the patent agent or associate patent agent for any application or patent for which the withdrawing agent was previously appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request succession the successor must provide a statement that they are the successor pursuant to section 32. Unless the Office receives contrary instructions the succession will be applied to all impacted applications and patents (including ones beyond reinstatement period and lapsed/expired patents). If multiple successors exist, each must submit documentation and indicate which applications/patents they intend to assume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation requirements — who may act during prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent agent is appointed to represent the applicant(s), or if there is a requirement to appoint one, the appointed patent agent must take action on behalf of the applicant(s) during the prosecution phase; the appointed agent could be the patent agent or the associate agent; where all agents at a firm are appointed any individual agent may represent the applicant(s) during prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent agent is not required and there is a single applicant/inventor, the single applicant must represent themself; for joint applicants/inventors they must be represented by the common representative (subsection 36(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Major prosecution actions that must be taken by appointed agent when one is appointed
rubrics_metrics.description: Some major actions must be taken by the appointed patent agent if one is appointed or required; these include responding to an examiner’s requisition, responding to a compliance notice under section 65 of the Patent Rules, and reinstating an application that has been abandoned for any reason other than failure to pay a maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections 5.07.01a and 5.07.02 for exceptions and other permitted representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation by others and 'persons authorized' rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions exist where applicants may represent themselves and where other persons may represent applicants even if a patent agent is appointed. Some actions may be permitted by 'persons authorized' by an applicant, patentee, or common representative; the Office does not require evidence of that authorization and will assume the person is authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of authorization is required when a registered foreign practitioner is signing the appointment of a patent agent, signing a small entity declaration, or requesting an interview with a patent examiner (subsections 27, 44 and 39).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an application, pay application fee, or effect PCT national entry
rubrics_metrics.description: The following persons may file an application, pay the application fee, or in PCT national phase cases satisfy requirements for national entry and pay associated fees (subsection 36(2)): the appointed patent agent; the applicant (any applicant if joint); any person authorized by any of the applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may pay annual maintenance fees for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual maintenance fees for applications and corresponding late fees may be paid by the appointed patent agent; the applicant (any applicant if joint); or any person authorized by any of the applicants (subsection 36(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may pay other fees relating to an application
rubrics_metrics.description: All other fees related to a patent application, such as the final fee, may be paid by the appointed patent agent, the single applicant, or the common representative (subsection 36(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may sign a small entity declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: A small entity declaration may be signed by the appointed patent agent; the applicant (any applicant if joint); or a registered foreign practitioner authorized by the applicant if a document showing proof of authorization (signed by the applicant) is submitted (paragraph 44(3)(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 5.07.03d for who can sign with respect to a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may reinstate an application abandoned for failure to pay maintenance fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application has been deemed abandoned for failure to pay a maintenance fee, the necessary steps to reinstate the application (outlined in paragraph 73(3)(a) of the Patent Act) may be taken by the appointed patent agent or by the single applicant or common representative (subsection 36(5)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit a request to record a transfer (single applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a single applicant, a request to record the transfer under subsection 49(2) may be submitted by the appointed patent agent, the applicant, or any person authorized by the applicant (subsection 36(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit a request to record a transfer (joint applicants — single applicant rights transferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are joint applicants and the rights of a single joint applicant are being transferred, a request to record the transfer may be submitted by: the appointed patent agent; the common representative; a person authorized by the common representative; the joint applicant whose rights are being transferred; any person authorized by that joint applicant (subsection 36(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit a request to record a transfer (joint applicants — multiple applicants' rights transferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are joint applicants and the rights of multiple joint applicants are being transferred, a request to record the transfer may be submitted by: the appointed patent agent; the common representative; any person authorized by the common representative (subsection 36(3)).
